newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South Africa's all-share index ended at an all-time high on Wednesday, its second consecutive closing peak boosted by a strong recovery on Wall Street on Tuesday and better-than-expected local inflation data.

Dealers said that the announcement after the market's close of a 200,000 foreign investment limit on individuals, a figure long awaited by the country, was seen neutral influence for stocks on Thursday despite the cap being higher than expected.

"I do not see an immediate effect. Investors now have a number of options. They are not going to rush in and take money offshore. They will make an informed investment decision," said James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollak.

Dealers said players would closely the rand's reaction to the further easing in foreign exchange controls, which takes effect on July 1, but that gold and foreign reserves were seen able to cope with any possible pressure on the currency.
Stock trade on Wednesday was volatile with volumes boosted by large trades in Corpgro and Consmining. Wooltru "N" shares and Murray and Roberts also saw good volumes.
"We have seen some active trade especially in index stocks. We have seen strong local buys in Wooltru N shares and Murray and Roberts," Scott said.

Dealers said May consumer inflation data's 9.5 percent year-on-year rise, which was slightly lower than economists' forecasts, was welcomed by the market and was another signpost for a possible cut soon in interest rates.
This boosted interest-rate sensitive shares, notably banking stocks, propelling the financial index to a fresh high of 10,124.0 -- a gain of 43.9 points.
The all-share index finished up 20.4 points to a record 7,354.0 points and the industrial index added 45.7 points to 8,669.9 -- its highest level since January 29, 1996.
Corpgro ended up two cents to 28 cents in a volume of over seven million shares and Consmining lost two cents to 61 cents in a volume of nearly 17 million shares.

Murray and Roberts shed 45 cents to 11 rand in a volume of nearly three million shares boosted by a two million share bookover. Wooltru ends down seven cents in a volume worth 67 million shares in a local buy.
Gold shares remained in negative territory as the bullion price hovererd around the $338 per ounce level.
"Golds are languishing still. There is so much uncertainty on them. One gets a feeling that the gold price is nearing bottom," Scott said.
The index ended down 11.2 points, or 1.1 percent, to 1,007.4 points.
The market was seen firm on Thursday ahead of the unit trust quarter end on Friday.
Other features included Pepkor which rose 145 cents to 25.25 rand after its sale of ailing stationer Waltons to investment group Bidvest and Investec Bank.
Investec ended down 150 cents at 179.50 rand and Bidvest was 35 cents down to 34.70 rand after rising to a record 35.35 rand earlier. Waltons' parent Walhold leapt 30 cents to 915 cents.

Sentrachem shares slipped, unimpressed by a major restructuring plan announced on Tuesday which would see it cut its debt by one billion rand in the next 12 to 18 months. It ended down 12 cents to 858 cents.

Near dated equity index futures were strong in late trade after the Dow Jones index leapt 153 points on Tuesday, retracing most of its hefty losses after a major sell-off the night before. The gold contract was a touch weaker, weighed by a dull bullion price.
The September all-share contract was last at 6,755/65 from 6,729, the industrial contract was at 8,482/89 from 8,381 and the gold contract was at 702/05 from 708.
-- Charles Phahlane, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
